title: Prove exact dyadic cyclic balancing and grid cost (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped all-length proof with exact finite corroboration. For dyadic diagonal balancing of a weighted cyclic recurrence to coefficient cap beta, put d_i=ceil(log_2(|a_i|/beta)).

```text
sum d_i > 0:  no dyadic balancing exists
sum d_i <= 0: minimum scale span = max(0, proper cyclic interval sums)
```

An explicit suffix-sum constructor attains the minimum. The least diagonal condition number is exactly 2^H. With minimum scale exponent zero, direct rescaling of arbitrary binary-grid inputs needs H additional common-grid fractional bits, and reverse scaling has sharp error gain 2^H.

For a=(2^k,2^(-k-2)) at cap 1/2, H=k+1. For a=(3/5,2/5), real scales attain cap 1/2 but no dyadic scales do, despite a strict product margin. These are scoped proofs, not search failures or a complete multiplication theorem. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Sricharan Vagvala / theon199's [PR1481](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1481), head 753c1b60eaf6ef464e258ca1fc022e53b5032cff, for Open next question 2 and its weighted expansive-cycle setting; Chafik Boukhalfa / PR628 and PR905, Charles Bethin / PR764, and the retained cyclic-kernel/precision lineage. Difference constraints and longest-path potentials are classical; general optimization or literature priority is unclaimed. The predecessor's scientific verifier was not replayed.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19362963). The delivered result is the scale-range and grid-cost subproblem; the full physical balancing invoice remains open.

## Evidence

Before, PR1481 left the scaling and two-grid cost of balancing unresolved. After, the written theorem gives the exact dyadic minimum and an attaining construction for every length.

Local CPython 3.12.15 checks pass at head 25d72c368430c2e5ab494de6bef6ade08fde9b8c:

- 19,530 demand vectors, including 10,886 feasible constructors. Exhaustive smaller-span optimization covers all 445 feasible cases through length four and rejects all 5,428 smaller candidate vectors.
- 5,600 rational coefficient/cap cases; every basis column of all 2,159 feasible conjugacies passes, totaling 8,255 columns and 32,005 entries.
- 25,000 coordinate grid checks, 1,110 sharp grid/error witnesses, 402 logarithmic ceiling boundary checks, 64 expansive-family members and 17 rejection or semantic controls.
- Both registered warning-strict normal and optimized commands pass and emit identical generated source-hash receipts. Each timed command finished in under one second, within its 120-second cap.
- Package metadata, registered replay, exact committed bytes/modes and source-history checks pass. Official six-file export integrity and input coverage pass. Optimized replay of the read-only export with Git absent from PATH produces the same receipt.
- Syntax/function-size inspection and staged whitespace checks pass. No separate static analyzer is claimed.

From the repository root, reproduce with this local interpreter path or substitute another CPython 3.12 executable:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/dyadic-cycle-balancing/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/dyadic-cycle-balancing/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/dyadic-cycle-balancing
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/dyadic-cycle-balancing --check-source-history --check-modes
```

The direct marker is PASS_DYADIC_CYCLE_BALANCING. The runner reports PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE, and publication preflight reports PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES. Receipts are generated, not handwritten or committed. Canonical main was refreshed unchanged before publication at 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a, priority revision 8.

## Limitations

The universal assertion rests on the written proof, supported by the finite domains. Complex phases are covered by the proof; conjugacy fixtures use signed real rationals. The implementation has explicit finite capacities.

Relative grid span and norm transfer do not establish an optimal rounded solver. Nonuniform grids, different algorithms and non-dyadic scales may change the cost. Physical scale instructions, reversible acquisition, arbitrary dirty restoration, complete numerical heights, scratch, tape/storage, coefficient preparation, the complete supplier invoice and selected-caller admission remain unproved. All five selected assumptions remain. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Lean, Docker and selected scientific cold replay were not run; every registered command ran locally.

## Open next questions

1. Build one reversible balanced cyclic inverse with explicit nonuniform grids, scaling instructions, rounded errors and complete restoration/movement costs.
2. Bind the exact minimum span to one actual coefficient table, cap and caller, then compare its complete precision/storage allowance.

## Related open work

No open PR on this exact dyadic balancing minimum was found in the inspected live PR bodies, handoffs and targeted searches. Sparse notes, arbitrary diffs and unpublished work remain coverage limits.

- [PR6426](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6426) studies degree growth of polynomial cyclic inverse row norms. This result concerns diagonal balancing of weighted first-order recurrences and computes no shared value. No additional computation was run to check that work.

The completion refresh covered this account's twelve open PRs created since the advance CLAIM, including this PR. The eleven others, PR6460 through PR6471 excluding PR6468, concern nilpotent-Schur and characteristic-five replay, a ternary COPY floor, helper-channel capacities, a stopped-recursion coefficient, tensor reconstruction, observable-mask preparation, a fixed matcher, triangular parity cuts and compatible fitting flags. None studies this dyadic balancing minimum or reports a competing value computed here. No additional mathematical computation was run to check those contributions.

No CI failure required repair.
